[MrFizz] Team, i’m looking at getting my first mirrorless camera. Looking at the Canon R50 twin lens kit to get me started. Any thoughts and advice would be greatly appreciated.
[MrFizz] Thanks for your input @niknikniknik. The +$500 this costs is just a bit too much of a stretch for me at this stage for my first camera. My budget was ~$1000 (very low I know) so getting to the Canon R50 was already a stretch.
[Lps] Are you wanting the camera for hobby use or productive purposes?
[MrFizz] @Lps: Just hobby, every chance I find I don't like/use it and I'm selling it in 12 months…
[7ekn00] @MrFizz: The R50 will frustrate the hell out of you :/
You will try indoor shots / video and wonder why they are so blurry/dark/grainy …
This is a much much much better option for flexibility (range of uses that it won't suck in)!
[MrFizz] @7ekn00: I feel like you people are a bad influence on my spending habits…
[Thayer] @MrFizz: This will have a better resale.
Though I would suggest other big deals are possibly also around the corner.
[MrFizz] @Thayer: Best to hold off for closer to Black friday?
[7ekn00] @MrFizz: Up to you, give the R50 a go - there is a chance your use case will be fine for it …
The R50 has a small sensor with really bad glass as standard :/ The above would be at least 4 stops better than the R50!
Although, if you use the R50 + kit lens with plenty of lighting, you will be fine (especially if all you are used to are crappy phone images / videos - the R50 should run rings around those) ;)
[Bobbson Jagnut] For your first camera - Go second hand DSLR and you’ll get a great body and multiple fantastic lenses for that budget.
An R50 doesn’t even have the best feature of mirrorless cameras - in body stabilisation (IBIS).
Canon RF lenses are also heeella expensive and you will probably buy EF lenses (canon DSLR lenses) and an adapter anyway.
If you really wanna go budget mirrorless, go secondhand Sony. The A73 is full frame (vs crop sensor r50) stabilised (r50 not so), has heaps of cheap lenses out there (R series are hella expensive) and goes for less money
But honestly even a cheap canon from 2013 will take fantastic photos in the right hands. Good luck with your photography journey, it will be well worth the practise, the struggle and learning curve.
[MrFizz] @Bobbson Jagnut: I'm flip flopping between super keen and ready to pull the trigger to it being all to complicated to get off the ground so just walk away :/
Knowing close to nothing, buying a second hand feels a bit risky that I'll buy a dud not knowing what I'm looking at…
[Bobbson Jagnut] @MrFizz: That is completely valid. And ya know what, the r50 is a good camera, just underwhelming for its price point. We’re ozbargainers so I’m very fussy with value. All the whacky features - there’s a lot that can overwhelm a newcomer.
IMO - you can safely spend like 300ish bucks on a canon 600D plus lens on marketplace and be chilling. Great camera, will produce fantastic pics, lots of EF lenses secondhand.
Otherwise if you wanna go safer. You can get nice 2nd hand cameras on eBay. Look for the ones from Japanese sellers that offer free shipping and returns. They are always in fantastic condition.
Or worse case you can overpay for 2nd hand Ted’s lol but they will have a warranty and will be cheaper to start than going brand new.
You can get a Nikon ZFC mirrorless camera for 1k @ Ted’s - not amazing value but it’s an awesome camera.
And feel free to use AI to help you digest all thennew information. Good luck and remember the most important thing is starting. Don’t let perfection stop you from taking up this awesome hobby.
[MrFizz] @Bobbson Jagnut: Thanks so much mate, you're effort and time are appreciated!
[Bobbson Jagnut] @MrFizz: If I could help ya more I would. Let me know if you have any questions.
[MrFizz] @Bobbson Jagnut: Any way I can send you a DM?
[Bobbson Jagnut] @MrFizz: I think you can tap on my name and send a message! I just tried sending one to you.
[SetTheFaqUp] @Bobbson Jagnut:
Go second hand DSLR and you’ll get a great body and multiple fantastic lenses for that budget.
Very good advice.
Get a Canon 5DII/III with a 24-70mm 2.8 to get started.
Nikon D610 can be had for cheap too.
[Bearlion] why would anyone go something other than canon or nikkon?
[7ekn00] Cause Sony run circles around both (for quality, dynamic range, AF, video) and Panasonic are far more usable whilst being cheaper :P
[SeanConnery] S5II has an active fan. If you shoot 4K video on a summer day, it's a lifesaver.
[Bobbson Jagnut] You probably can’t go wrong with either. I love the Sony mirrorless cameras, they’re so compact and sigma makes great lenses. Also, there are so many great E mount lenses for excellent prices.
But I know a guy who swears by his lumix (because he gets a lot of value out of taking videos).
Good luck and have fun
